questions.text: As a British citizen what are your responsibilities (choose two answers)?
questions.explanation: If you wish to be a permanent resident or citizen of the UK, you should:respect and obey the law, look after yourself and your family, respect the rights of others, including their right to their own opinions, treat others with fairness and look after the area in which you live and the environment.

options.text: To respect and obey the law
To walk your dog only during the day
To go to church on Sunday
To look after yourself and your family

questions.text: Who made the first coins to be minted in Britain?
questions.explanation: Thepeople of the Iron Agemade the first coins to be minted in Britain, some inscribed with the names of Iron Age kings. This marks the beginnings of British history.

options.text: The people of the Stone Age
The people of the Iron Age

questions.text: Who built the Tower of London?
questions.explanation: The correct answer isWilliam the Conqueror.

questions.text: There are 15 national parks in England, Wales and Scotland. What are national parks?
questions.explanation: National Parks areareas of protected countryside that everyone can visit, and where people live, work and look after the landscape.

options.text: Land formations of columns made from volcanic lava

questions.text: Northern Ireland has its own established church.
questions.explanation: False. There is no established Church in Wales or Northern Ireland.

questions.text: Which three territories form Great Britain?
questions.explanation: ‘Great Britain’ refers only to England, Scotland and Wales,nottoNorthern Ireland.

questions.text: How often are ’Prime Minister’s Questions’ held in the parliament?
questions.explanation: Prime Minister’s Questions takes placeevery weekwhile Parliament is sitting.

questions.text: Which king was executed in 1649?
questions.explanation: The correct answer isCharles I.

questions.text: Where was William Shakespeare born?
questions.explanation: Shakespeare was born inStratford-upon-Avon, England.

questions.text: Which two of the following are famous British Paralympians?
questions.explanation: Baroness Tanni Grey-ThompsonandEllie Simmondsare the correct answers.

questions.text: Who was reigning in England when English settlers first began to colonise the eastern coast of America?
questions.explanation: InElizabeth I’s time, English settlers first began to colonise the eastern coast of America.

questions.text: Scotland and Wales use a system called ‘individual registration’ where all those entitled to vote must complete their own registration form.
questions.explanation: False. Northern Irelanduses a system called ‘individual registration’ and all those entitled to vote must complete their own registration form.

questions.text: On what day is the birth of Jesus Christ celebrated?
questions.explanation: Christmas Day, 25th of December, celebrates the birth of Jesus Christ.

questions.text: What sort of battle was the ’Battle of Britain’, fought between Germany and Britain in the summer of 1940?
questions.explanation: ‘The Battle of Britain’ was a crucialaerial battlefought between Germany and Britain in the summer of 1940.

questions.text: Where is Swansea located?
questions.explanation: Swansea it is located inWales.

questions.text: Which two political parties formed a coalition in 2010?
questions.explanation: In May 2010the Conservative and Liberal Democrat partiesformed a coalition and the leader of the Conservative Party, David Cameron, became Prime Minister.

questions.text: Who established the Church of England?
questions.explanation: The correct answer isHenry VIII.

questions.text: In 1348, one third of the population in England, Wales and Scotland died as a result of which disease?
questions.explanation: In 1348, a disease, probably a form of plague, came to Britain. This was known asthe Black Death. One third of the population of England died and a similar proportion in Scotland and Wales.

questions.text: Haggis is a traditional food from which area?
questions.explanation: Haggis is a traditional food fromScotland.

questions.text: Which court deals with minor criminal offences in Scotland?
questions.explanation: In Scotland, minor criminal offences go to aJustice of the Peace Court.

options.text: The Justice of the Peace Court

questions.text: Which two of the following records give us information about England during the reign of William I?
questions.explanation: The Domesday Book and the Bayeux Tapestry.

questions.text: Which two documents do you need to apply for a National Insurance number?
questions.explanation: To apply for a National Insurance number you needdocuments that prove your identity and that you have permission to work in the UK.

options.text: A document with your address on it, such as a tenancy agreement
